answer: Identity is accrued, not claimed. A newcomer stakes collateral in a shared vault and then serves a probation window where its rewards sit escrowed while peers contest its work history; a gale of cloned registrations each pays that toll separately and forfeits it at the first contradiction, so mass-producing identities costs more than the reach it buys. Trust then thickens like a reef, layer upon verified layer that no fresh key can inherit.
